title: One Button Beats Every Override: Parent Lock for YouTube | vitalii.no
description:
How a single admin switch finally lets a parent shut off YouTube and Spotify no matter which override is currently active.

A home kiosk setup already had an override for almost everything: a free-viewing mode, a parent's timed QR pass, even a finished bonus quiz that unlocked apps as a reward. Each one worked fine on its own, but there was no single switch to just say no regardless of which override happened to be live. If a parent wanted tier-2 apps off right now, they first had to remember and undo whichever exception was currently active.

The fix is one admin button that POSTs to the youtube-gate Worker, guarded so only a parent's own session can flip it. The endpoint writes a dedicated settings flag, kept deliberately separate from the normal gate state so a lock, a master-off, or the nightly cutoff can never accidentally wipe it out. On every status check, that flag is read first and forces YouTube and Spotify closed ahead of every other rule — the free-viewing mode, the QR pass, even an already-finished bonus — so this one flag outranks all of them.

The result: a parent can now shut every tier-2 app from their phone with one tap, and it holds no matter what else is unlocked — the one override that was missing from a system that already had an override for everything.
